title: Pressure history cut Atlantic wind-change error but gave uncertain eastern Pacific gains in 2002-2025 tests
abstract: We tested current central pressure and its past 12-hour change as added predictors of next-day wind change, beyond storm state and wind history. Models used earlier seasons only, from 1982. For 3,636 starts from 260 Atlantic storms, added pressure history cut mean squared error by 5.32%. The two-basin family-adjusted conditional interval was 2.06% to 8.23%. For 4,684 starts from 348 eastern Pacific storms, the gain was 2.34%, with limits of -3.20% to 4.87%. The Pacific result changed with coastal screening and model penalty. The primary result supports added Atlantic information, but gives no clear Pacific gain. This is a retrospective model test, not a test of physical cause or real-time skill. Revised best tracks, linked wind and pressure estimates, future sample screening, longitude extrapolation and conditional uncertainty limit use. Code, aggregate evidence, source hashes, an audit and a figure are included. Source records remain external.

display.caption: Pressure-history skill and planned checks. Bars show ordinary 95% conditional season-block intervals. Family-adjusted primary limits are in the text.
